documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

46 yo M establishing care. Prior PCP retiring. Main issue is blood pressure: told he had high BP around 2016, started on lisinopril and later HCTZ added. Takes both most mornings, admits he misses some. No home cuff. Uses ibuprofen 200 mg, one or two, for headaches maybe once a week, bought OTC. No chest pain, no SOB, no swelling.

PMH: hypertension. No surgeries.
Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, HCTZ 25 daily, ibuprofen 200 prn.
Allergies: none to medications.
FHx: father has diabetes and high blood pressure and had heart trouble; mother overweight with high BP; one brother.
SHx: married. Construction site supervisor, long days outdoors. Says he has a cigar now and then when out with friends, no cigarettes he will own to. Drinks socially, "a couple on the weekend." No drugs. Eats on the road a lot.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: BP and pulse in flowsheet; BP high again on recheck. Well appearing, heavyset. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abd soft, nontender. Ext without edema, pulses 2+ symmetric. Skin no rash.

Assessment/plan:
1. Essential hypertension - above goal today on two drugs. He thinks it is the coffee and the drive in. Keep lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 for now, asked him to take them every day without skipping. Recheck at his physical. CMP today.
2. Health maintenance - Tdap today (last tetanus he can't recall). Hep C and HIV screening offered, accepted. CBC with the chemistry. Colon screening discussed, prefers to talk about it at the physical.
3. Tobacco/alcohol - minimal by his account. AUDIT-C 3. Will revisit.
4. Records release signed for prior office.

Physical in the spring, sooner if anything comes up.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Patrick, your blood work came back fine. Kidney function, potassium and blood counts are normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change. Keep taking both blood pressure pills every day and we will look at the numbers again at your physical.

ANNUAL EXAM

47M, here fasting. Feels fine. No complaints. Took his BP pills this morning. Ibuprofen now and then for headaches, nothing new about them.

Interval: none.
FHx update: father had an MI at 52. Also has diabetes and HTN. Mother obesity and HTN.
Social: still says only an occasional cigar at a get-together. Alcohol "only socially." Works long hours, eats whatever is on the site.

ROS: negative x 12 systems.

Exam:
Vitals per flowsheet. BP 142/88, HR 78. BMI 29.
Gen: well, in no distress.
HEENT: normal. Neck: no adenopathy, thyroid normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur or gallop.
Resp: clear to auscultation.
Abd: soft, non-tender, no organomegaly.
Ext: warm, no edema.
Skin: unremarkable.
Neuro: grossly intact.
Impression: normal exam.

Labs this AM: TC 220, HDL 35, LDL 150, TG 175. FBG 96.

A/P:
- Metabolic syndrome: BP on treatment, low HDL, high triglycerides. Glucose normal today but strong family history of diabetes. Referring to endocrinology to assess diabetes risk and talk prevention. Diet and activity counseling given - fewer drive-through lunches, walk evenings.
- Mixed hyperlipidemia: as above, lifestyle first.
- HTN: 142/88, still above goal. Same regimen, he promises to be more consistent.
- CRC screening: chose FIT, kit given.
- PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 3.
- Flu declined in the fall. COVID vaccine - plans to get it at the pharmacy when eligible.

RTC 6 mo or after endo.

documents.title: Your physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Patrick - fasting sugar was normal at 96. Cholesterol pattern is the one we talked about: good cholesterol low at 35, triglycerides 175, LDL 150. Together with your blood pressure that is what we call metabolic syndrome. Endocrinology will call you to schedule. Don't forget to mail back the stool kit.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION LETTER
Date of service: 06/21/2021
Re: Patrick Carlson, DOB 02/10/1974

Thank you for referring Mr. Carlson for evaluation of diabetes risk in the setting of metabolic syndrome.

He is a 47-year-old construction site supervisor with hypertension of roughly five years' duration, currently on lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide. He reports smoking about one and a half packs per day for 30 years. He does not exercise on a regular basis and eats fast food on most days of the week. Father with type 2 diabetes.

Medications: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, ibuprofen 200 mg as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 138/88. BMI 30. Remainder of a focused exam was unremarkable; no acanthosis, thyroid not enlarged.

Labs today: fasting glucose 105 mg/dL, hemoglobin A1c 5.9%.

Impression: Prediabetes, in the setting of metabolic syndrome.

Recommendations:
1. We discussed his risk of progressing to type 2 diabetes and what lowers it: modest weight loss of 5 to 7 percent, 150 minutes a week of activity, cutting sugared drinks and fried food. Referral information for a diabetes prevention program given.
2. Smoking raises his cardiometabolic risk further; cessation strongly encouraged.
3. No pharmacotherapy at this time. Repeat A1c in 6 to 12 months through your office.
4. Follow-up here as needed.

Sincerely,
Endocrinology

documents.title: Endocrinology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got the letter from endocrinology. A1c 5.9 puts you in the prediabetes range, not diabetes. The plan is the lifestyle piece - some weight off, more walking, less fast food - and a repeat A1c here in 6 to 12 months. They also told you what I will keep telling you about the smoking. Did you get the prevention program info?

documents.title: Cardiology Office Note
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY PRACTICE - OFFICE NOTE
Visit date: 03/24/2022
Patient: Carlson, Patrick  DOB 02/10/1974
Referring: primary care

Reason: BP management, weight gain.

HPI: 48M with HTN, metabolic syndrome and prediabetes followed by endocrinology, referred for blood pressure that remains hard to control. States he is taking hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril as prescribed. Concerned about weight - up about 10 lb in the last 6 months by his estimate. No exertional chest symptoms, palpitations, syncope or orthopnea.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, ibuprofen PRN.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: 30 pack-years of cigarettes. Drinks socially on weekends. Diet heavy in processed food; exercises infrequently.
Family: father with premature coronary disease, diabetes and HTN.

Exam: BP 146/92, HR 78, regular. BMI 32. Waist 102 cm. JVP not elevated. S1 S2 normal, no murmurs, rubs or gallops. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft. No edema; distal pulses intact.

Labs: Na 140, K 3.8, Cr 1.1. Fasting glucose 102. Total cholesterol 210, HDL 35, LDL 145, TG 150.

Assessment:
1. Essential hypertension, suboptimally controlled.
2. Metabolic syndrome.
3. Tobacco use.

Plan: Counseled on weight reduction, sodium restriction under 2 g/day, DASH-pattern eating, and a goal of 30 minutes of brisk activity most days. Continue lisinopril and HCTZ at current doses. Keep a home BP log for 2 to 4 weeks and send to PCP. Smoking cessation strongly advised. Return to cardiology as needed.

Received by fax 08/16/2022 after request.

documents.title: Follow-up / Tobacco Counseling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48 yo M, metabolic syndrome, HTN, prediabetes per endo last year. Here to go over labs and to talk about smoking, which he asked to do.

Smoking: tells me today it's a pack a day, and has been for about 30 years - more than the cigars he mentioned before. Has been thinking about quitting for the past year but hasn't set a date or tried anything. Gets that it's bad for him with his BP and his dad's heart. Has quit cold turkey before and was back within a couple of weeks each time. Worried he can't do it with the job.

Labs 8/30: A1c 7.8, fasting glucose 172. TC 210, HDL 35, LDL 145, TG 250.

Exam: BP 142/88. BMI 31. Obese abdomen, otherwise unremarkable - heart regular, lungs clear, no edema, feet with intact skin and sensation.

A/P
1. Type 2 diabetes, new - A1c 7.8 and fasting 172 on the same draw. Explained what this means and that it is common with his family history. Starting metformin 500 mg BID with food, will go to 1000 BID in a month if his stomach handles it. Glucose meter and strips sent; check fasting a few mornings a week. Diabetes education referral info given. Eye exam and urine albumin at the next visit.
2. Tobacco use disorder - contemplation. Spent ~10 min: personal risk, what withdrawal looks like, the quitline number. Offered nicotine patch plus short-acting NRT or varenicline. He wants to cut down on his own first and will let me know. Not starting anything today.
3. Obesity, BMI 31 - with the diabetes, weight loss is the best lever. Talked portion size and drinks.
4. HTN - 142/88, same meds.
5. Prediabetes resolved -> diabetes.

RTC 3 months with A1c.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PHYSICAL - 49M

HPI: Here for physical, missed June DM visit. Taking metformin. BP meds "usually." Smoking around half a pack to a pack depending on the week. Never sent the FIT back - kit expired; we'll restart that next year.

Alcohol: asked directly today. "A few beers most nights" after work, more on weekends. AUDIT-C 7. Says his wife has been after him to cut back. Doesn't see it as a problem but agreed to talk to someone about it.

ROS: no chest pain, no dyspnea, no GI bleeding, no jaundice, no edema. Mood "fine." PHQ-2 1.

Exam: BP 144/90 (flowsheet). Gen well. HEENT nl. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Feet intact, sensation normal. Skin no rash.

Labs today (resulted same afternoon, added to note): A1c 7.1. AST 62, ALT 47. Rest of CMP fine. CBC unremarkable.

A/P
1. Alcohol use - by his account well above low-risk limits; liver enzymes now up, AST more than ALT. Referral to outpatient psychiatry for an alcohol use evaluation, he accepts. Asked him to cut down in the meantime.
2. T2DM - A1c 7.1 on metformin 1000 BID. Continue. Eye exam still not done.
3. HTN - 144/90. Take them every day.
4. Tobacco - not ready.
5. Health maint: FIT next year. Shingles vaccine at 50.

RTC 6 mo.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Patrick, A1c held at 7.1. The liver tests (AST 62, ALT 47) are elevated, and with the drinking we talked about that's the most likely reason. That's part of why I want the psychiatry evaluation. Their office should call you within a couple of weeks.

documents.title: Psychiatry Evaluation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY - INITIAL EVALUATION
Visit: 09/21/2023
Patient: Patrick Carlson, 49 y/o male
Referral source: PCP, alcohol use evaluation

Identifying information: Married man who supervises construction crews, seen with his wife at his request.

History: He opened by describing "a few beers" after work to unwind. On more detailed questioning he acknowledged six beers every weekday evening and frequently more on weekends. He maintains that drinking has no impact on his job or his marriage. His wife, present for part of the interview, disagreed with visible worry: she described him as more irritable in recent months and said they have argued several times about the drinking. He mentions intermittent stress at work. Smokes about half a pack of cigarettes daily by his report. Medical history per referral: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, tobacco use, obesity.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, ibuprofen PRN. NKDA.
Family psychiatric history: brother with alcohol use disorder.

Mental status: Alert, cooperative though guarded on the topic of alcohol. Speech normal rate. Mood "fine"; affect mildly irritable when his wife spoke. Thought process linear. Denies SI/HI. No perceptual disturbance. Insight limited; judgment fair.

Vitals: BP 140/90, HR 88, BMI 29.
Physical findings: liver edge palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin; spider angiomas over the upper torso.

Labs drawn today: GGT 95 U/L (ref 9-48), MCV 96 fL (ref 80-96), AST 70 U/L (ref 10-40), ALT 50 U/L (ref 7-56).

Assessment: Alcohol use disorder. Laboratory and examination findings are consistent with heavy ongoing alcohol use. Minimization noted.

Plan:
- Feedback given on the link between his drinking, the exam findings and labs. Recommended stopping or, at minimum, substantially reducing intake.
- Offered follow-up visits here and information on community support groups; he will "think about it."
- Will defer further medical evaluation to primary care.

Copy to PCP.

REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN NOTE (abbreviated)
Arrival 03/13/2025 17:40
51M with HTN, DM2, metabolic syndrome, tobacco and alcohol use.

CC: headaches in the morning, tired, short of breath with exertion.

HPI: Several months of dull headaches across both sides of the head, worst on waking, slowly getting worse. Also more winded on stairs than he used to be. No chest pain, palpitations, recent illness, visual change, dizziness or weakness. HTN for several years; has not kept up with follow-up. Reports taking only HCTZ and not every day. Eats a lot of salt. No regular exercise. 1 ppd. Drinks on weekends per pt.

VS: BP 188/106, P 84, RR 18.
Exam: Heart sounds normal. Mild crackles at both bases. Abdomen benign. Neuro nonfocal. Visual acuity normal. Fundi: arteriolar narrowing and AV nicking both eyes; no hemorrhage, exudate or disc swelling.
ECG and chest film: no acute findings.

Impression: Uncontrolled hypertension; hypertensive retinopathy.
Disposition: Discharged. Instructed to take lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide every day as prescribed, low-salt diet. Follow up with PCP within 1 week.

NKDA.

documents.title: Urgent Visit - Medications / Glucose
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in on a same-day slot after a text from his wife. First visit since 2/2024. ED in March for BP 188/106 with hypertensive retinopathy, then missed the follow-up.

He has not been taking the lisinopril or HCTZ - stopped after a few weeks following the ED, "felt fine." Takes metformin most days. Not checking sugars, meter is "somewhere." Smoking a pack a day, about 30 years. He says he knows he has to do something about his health. Not sure he can quit smoking or drop weight, has tried both. Wants to understand what each change would actually buy him and how hard it would be.

Labs 9/8: A1c 8.2, fasting glucose 176. TC 220, HDL 32, LDL 145, TG 250. Liver enzymes still up, similar to 2023. Kidney function and urine albumin normal.

Exam: BP 152/96. BMI 32. Acanthosis nigricans at the back and sides of the neck. Otherwise unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema, feet intact with normal monofilament.

A/P
1. Medication nonadherence / HTN uncontrolled. We went through what untreated pressure has already done to his eyes and can do to heart, brain and kidneys. Capacity: he can describe his conditions and the risks of leaving them untreated in his own words, weighs them against what he sees as the cost, and gives the same answer each time I come back to it - he has capacity to make these decisions, and his choice today is to restart both BP pills and see how it goes. Lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 re-sent.
2. T2DM, A1c 8.2 - poorly controlled with missed doses and diet. Metformin 1000 BID, every day. Restart fasting checks 3x/week.
3. Tobacco - long talk on the benefits (BP, heart, lungs, cost) and the hard parts (withdrawal, work breaks). Still not ready for patches or a pill; knows they're available. Lung cancer screening CT ordered.
4. Alcohol - AUDIT-C 6, says it's "down." Encouraged further cutback; psychiatry offer stands.
5. Weight/acanthosis - goes with the insulin resistance. Discussed realistic first steps.
6. Eyes - ophthalmology referral for the retinopathy and his diabetic eye exam.
7. Flu shot today. PHQ-9 4.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up for HTN/DM/metabolic syndrome after last fall's visit about missed meds. I was held up with an urgent add-on and he waited over an hour. Visibly angry when I came in, raised his voice - he's been waiting, nobody seems to care, he has a job to get to. I apologized, didn't argue, sat down, and let him finish. He calmed within a few minutes and stayed for the visit. No other complaints today.

Meds: taking metformin. Occasional ibuprofen for headaches. Not taking lisinopril or HCTZ again - ran out after the September fill and didn't call.

Labs 3/9: fasting glucose 158, A1c 7.8 (8.2 in Sept). Cr 1.2. UA no protein or blood.

BP 160/100, HR 88. Exam otherwise unremarkable: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
1. Situational irritability/anger today, related to the wait. Resolved with acknowledgment. Will try to book him first slot of the day going forward.
2. HTN, uncontrolled, off meds again. Agrees to restart lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 today; refills sent. BMP 2 weeks after restarting (Cr 1.2 today).
3. T2DM, A1c 7.8. Metformin 1000 BID. Continue.
